Tuned Mercedes-AMG G 63 Will Instantly Tell People You're Loaded. Do You Like the (Larte) Design?
17 photos
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign
After taking on various different rides recently, including a few Mercedes-AMG G 63s , Larte Design continues its tuning frenzy with yet another take on the popular German premium super truck.
The project is simply called the Mercedes-AMG G 63 by Larte Design, and the visual updates are said to fit the 2025 to 2025 model year cars. The styling part is more than visible, and will immediately tell bystanders that they are looking at a very special G-Wagen, regardless of whether they have a petrolhead license in their wallet or not, as the add-ons are definitely in-your-face.
Starting at the front, we can see that the bumper has been altered during the tuning process. This modded Mercedes-AMG G 63 has new air vent trim, and a quite fat apron. The latter looks more like a diffuser than a splitter due to its multi-fin design, though, but it is not on the brash side of things. Or is it? Actually, that is for you to decide, yet before inviting you to leave your impression on this project, we also have to go through other details that make it more special.
For instance, the grille is also on the special side of things, as it sports a new pattern that combines both horizontal and vertical slats, in a design that looks like a mix between a Benz and an AMG. Larte Design’s logo hasn’t replaced the three-pointed star emblem in the middle of the new grille, and we (or I in this case) think that that is a win. The turn signals have been smoked, and they flank the new hood that sports a more aggressive design, and has a pair of nostrils at the front.
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign Further back, this tuned Mercedes-AMG G 63 is home to a roof attachment above the front windscreen, which holds a pair of light strips on each side. It looks like this machine also features power running boards for easier ingress and egress. The rear bumper looks like the stock element to us, but the diffuser attached to it is anything but OEM. It features extra brake lights on the sides, and seems to have a cutout in the middle for the tow hook.
The custom spare wheel holder attached to the rear door is also part of the makeover, and it features a different pattern, and has Larte Design’s logo on it. Usually, the side-exit tailpipes of the Mercedes-AMG G 63 also get modded whenever most tuners get their hands on this model, but in this case, we are not sure that they have. The wheels, however, are entirely new, and seem to be about as big as the standard ones.
Finished in brushed silver, they provide some contrast to the rest of the exterior, which features a satin green look that is likely a wrap. The body kit add-ons were crafted of carbon fiber, and some of them, like the hood for instance, have a dry carbon look that contributes to the tuned Mercedes-AMG G 63’s more special nature.
The interior hasn’t been detailed in the pictures that Larte Design shared on its social media channels, and that’s because this project is all about the visual upgrades on the outside. However,zooming in through the windows in certain images reveals that black is the color that dominates the cockpit.
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign Do you know what the tuner hasn’t mentioned? That’s right, the powertrain. And this obviously tells us that the oily bits haven’t been touched with the tuning stick. As a result, this Mercedes-AMG G 63 should still have 577 hp (430 kW/585 ps) and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque to play with. Unless it actually boasts more oomph, which we doubt.
The 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine allows the standard G 63 to hit 62 mph (100 kph) in 4.3 seconds from rest. The model has a top speed of up to 149 mph (240 kph), though in order to reach it, your modern-day AMG G-Wagen must have the optional AMG Driver’s Pack. Otherwise, the maximum speed will drop to 137 mph (220 kph), and that’s still more than enough for daily drives.
Larte Design hasn’t said anything about the pricing of this body kit at the time of writing, so if you want to find out how much it will cost you to make your new-age Mercedes-AMG G 63 looks like this, then you will have to reach out to the tuner directly. And if you do, feel free to tell us what the magical number is. By the way, don’t forget that these dry carbon elements are said to fit the 2025 to 2027 model year G 63.
Now, if you had such a thing and wanted to make it stand out more, would you actually opt for Larte Design’s bundle detailed above? I’d probably have second thoughts about it. View this post on Instagram A post shared by LARTE DESIGN | BODY KITS | WHEELS | AUTO DESIGN (@lartedesign)
